messages:
sara_sales: Hey team — SegNet (coastal fintech) just signed an NDA and wants a Private Deploy POC next sprint. Key asks: no general internet egress (only an allowlist of 3 FQDNs), preserve client source IP all the way to their app logs, KMS/HSM details for the security questionnaire, and a pricing estimate for POC -> production (they care about seat/license vs reserved capacity delta). Can we outline network options + firewall snippet we can share with their infra team?

alex_netops: Quick take — two viable topologies: VPC peering (cross-account peering) or PrivateLink (interface endpoints). Important tradeoffs: peering preserves client src IP, PrivateLink will SNAT traffic through our ENIs so srcIP is lost. If srcIP is mandatory for log correlation, lean peering.

jordan_solutions: +1 on peering for srcIP. For customers that can't accept peering we can offer a customer-managed NAT solution to pass through original IP via a proxy header, but that requires app changes (X-Forwarded-For).

nyla_security: For the security questionnaire: we support customer KMS integration (we can accept CMKs via AWS KMS with cross-account grants) and have an HSM-backed option for Enterprise tier. I'll draft the KMS/HSM answers and required artifacts. Also note: privatedeploy has audit logs export and optional SOC2 supplement.

sam_engineer: On pricing: POC options — 30d proof-of-concept with a temporary license (no platform fee, infra billed) or a discounted Reserved Private plan (we typically offer a 50% first-90-day discount on platform license for strategic deals). Production Reserved: monthly commit + seat license for Private deployments. I'll pull numbers and example SOW line items.

alex_netops: Firewall snippet we can share (AWS SG + iptables examples). The idea: restrict egress to the three FQDNs via proxy or SG+NACL. Example SG rule for customer outbound:

```
# AWS Security Group (egress) - allow only to Redwood FQDNs
Type: HTTPS  Protocol: TCP  Port Range: 443  Destination: <redwood-proxy-eip-1>/32, <redwood-proxy-eip-2>/32
# also permit DNS to resolver
Type: DNS    Protocol: UDP  Port Range: 53   Destination: <customer-dns-resolver>/32
```

If they insist on FQDN instead of IP, advise using an outbound HTTPS proxy that enforces FQDN allowlist (we can provide proxy IPs). For on-host iptables example to enforce allowlist via proxy:

```
# force all outbound to proxy
iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.10.10.5:3129
# allow proxy to reach Redwood
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d <redwood-proxy-eip-1> --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# drop everything else
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP
```

Note: preservering source IP across peering requires route table entries and no NAT on either side. If customer uses TGW and our deployment is in a different account, we need explicit route propagation and shared route tables.

jordan_solutions: One more gotcha — TLS inspection appliances will break certificate pinning. If their security team wants deep TLS inspection, we should document how to handle pinned certs and recommend mTLS between customer and our edge.

nyla_security: Regarding the questionnaire: they asked about key rotation, KMS access controls, and whether we store plaintext model inputs. Short answers: keys are customer-managed (we can do BYOK via KMS grants), rotation supported per KMS policy, and we do not persist plaintext inputs beyond processing unless configured for logging/analytics (opt-in). I'll produce the formal wording.

deploybot: Automated note: created ticket INFRA-9123 to track peering runbook + SG artifacts. Assignee: alex_netops. ETA: 2 business days.

sara_sales: Thanks — next steps: Alex, can you produce a one-page network playbook for the customer (peering + PrivateLink decision matrix + the SG/iptables snippets) by EOD tomorrow? Nyla, please attach KMS/HSM answers to the security questionnaire draft. Sam, attach POC pricing matrix with a clear line for "POC discount" and "Reserved Private monthly commit". I'll loop in the customer's infra lead once we have the doc. :thumbsup:

alex_netops: Will do. I'll include diagram options (peering architecture with route examples, PrivateLink flow with SNAT note) and a short checklist for their firewall team (DNS, NTP, proxy IPs, health-check endpoints).

sam_engineer: I'll draft the pricing table and include example numbers for 2 vCPU-equivalent / 1 Gpu-equivalent unit for comparison — won't commit final rates until legal/Sales Ops signs off.

sara_sales: Perfect. tagging @segnet-infra (external) once we have the docs.
